Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery — escalation SLAs & incident expectations

Thanks again for the call today — quick recap and proposed asks so we have a single thread to track items. High level takeaways:

- What you told us: primary concern is predictable incident behaviour (acknowledgement, mitigation) and clean RCAs you can pass to your SOC/review board. You called out two recent hyperscaler outages (region-level network flap / control plane fail) and asked how we compare before you commit to an onboarding timetable.
- Our differentiation: smart routing + prioritized failover, deterministic acknowledgement SLA for enterprise plans, and a lightweight RCA template we can auto-populate with telemetry. We also offer optional dedicated capacity for isolation.

Action items / asks from Nimbus: 
1) Confirm target SLA windows you need for acknowledgement and mitigation (e.g., 1h ack, 4h mitigation vs longer).
2) Confirm whether you need contractual RCA turnaround times (e.g., provisional RCA within 24h, full RCA within 7 business days).
3) Approve a short technical runbook test (we propose a controlled failover test against a reserved Dedicated pool + comparison to a hyperscaler-hosted endpoint).

Proposed next steps from our side:
- I have attached an SLA matrix (SLA-matrix.xlsx) comparing our targeted timelines vs typical hyperscaler behaviours; also attached a 1-page incident playbook summary (incident-playbook-summary.pdf).
- Jordan (cc'd) will sketch a lightweight test plan to validate ack/mitigation timings and telemetry completeness.
- If this looks good, we can lock a tentative slot the week of May 17 for a 90-120 minute technical session with your SREs.

If you can reply with the answers to 1–3 above, we will finalize the test plan and calendar invite.

Best,

Thanks, Sergio — quick answers and a couple of follow-ups: 

- Ack window: we need < 1 hour acknowledgement for any Sev 1 incidents (we can compromise to 1h if contractual).
- Mitigation: target is 4 hours for a full mitigation or clear mitigation plan; anything longer needs exec-level notification.
- RCA: provisional within 24h is preferred; final within 5 business days if possible.

Two asks from our end: 
1) Can you share two anonymized RCAs where the vendor demonstrated a mitigation path vs when a hyperscaler had a multi-hour outage? We want to see level of detail and telemetry.
2) Please call out any differences in support escalation paths — we currently have a two-tier path with hyperscalers (engineering + cloud infra) and want parity or better.

Appreciate the attachments; will review. If you could include a proposed test plan (even a checklist) that highlights how you would simulate control-plane vs network-flap like failures, that would help our SREs sign off.

– Ellie
Ellie Morgan

Subject: Re: Draft test plan for escalation / incident comparison (internal)

Folks — putting a concise test plan here so Sergio can share with Nimbus tomorrow. This is intentionally lightweight: goal is to measure acknowledgement time, mitigation start, and RCA completeness with identical simulated faults across three targets (Redwood Hosted, Redwood Dedicated, Hyperscaler endpoint).

Quick test outline:
- Test types (two scenarios):
  * Control-plane error: emulate token-service/control-plane unavailability for 6–10 minutes.
  * Network-flap: intermittent packet loss to a subset of nodes for 8–12 minutes.
- Targets: Redwood Hosted (region us-west-2), Redwood Dedicated (pre-provisioned pool for Nimbus), Hyperscaler API (customer-selected region).
- Metrics to capture: time-to-ack (email/SMS/pager), time-to-first-mitigation action, percent requests retried/succeeded, end-to-end latency spike, completeness of logs (request ids + kv cache traces).
- Success criteria: acknowledgement within 1h, mitigation plan initiated within 4h, post-test provisional RCA with required fields (timeline, root cause, mitigation steps, telemetry links) within 24h. Final RCA within 5 business days for the purposes of this PO.

Operational notes:
- We'll need a shared telemetry collection bucket (S3) and short-lived API keys for the hyperscaler test.
- Laura, can you confirm availability of a Dedicated pool for May 18–20? If not, we propose May 24–26.
- Ben, please prepare a neutral comparator matrix that lists expected behaviours and where automated fallback would kick in.

Attachment: escalation-test-plan.md (internal) — includes the checklist and exact scripts.

Jordan
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
